subject: Discovery recap + proposed pilot charter and evaluation approach (shadow vs offline)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Discovery recap + proposed pilot charter and evaluation approach (shadow vs offline)

Hi Claire / Trials team,

Thanks for a productive discovery earlier today. Quick recap and a proposed pilot charter so we can align on success gates and the evaluation methodology (I highlighted a decision we need from you in bold).

TL;DR proposed pilot: 4-week engagement — 2 weeks online shadowing + 2 weeks validation (offline scoring and focused pragmatic QA). Goal: demonstrate 1) net accuracy uplift on downstream triage tasks (entity extraction + routing), 2) maintain <200ms 95th latency on realistic traffic, and 3) total inference cost per 1k requests below $X (we'll calibrate once you share expected qps).

What we discussed / assumptions:
- Primary success metric: micro-F1 on the entity extraction extractor used in your triage workflow (we'll use your anonymized production samples).
- Secondary metrics: downstream routing precision, operator override rate, false positive rate for PHI tagging, and median/95th latency.
- Data access: you confirmed we can run shadow inference on a sample of live traffic with redaction and local-only logs. We still need the sample volume and retention constraints.

Proposed evaluation plan (two paths; pick one):
1) Online shadow (recommended for realistic signal)
   - Run Redwood inference side-by-side with your production system; we only log model outputs and evaluation metadata (no user-facing changes).
   - Duration: 2 weeks minimum; sample size target: ~10k user interactions across peak/off-peak.
   - Pros: captures real distribution, latency/throughput realism, accurate operator override measurement.
   - Cons: requires integration on routing layer and a short security review for redacted payloads.

2) Offline / synthetic evaluation
   - You provide labeled holdout datasets (we can augment with synthetic perturbations).
   - Duration: 1 week to run and iterate on scoring; we recommend 1–2 additional calibration passes.
   - Pros: fast, lower risk for data governance.
   - Cons: may over/underestimate live behavior for edge cases.

Suggested grading rubric (0-5 per category; pass threshold: weighted score >= 3.5):
- Accuracy (primary) — weight 40%
- Latency (95th) — weight 20%
- Safety / PHI redaction robustness — weight 15%
- Cost per 1k inference units — weight 15%
- Operational overhead (configs, monitoring, retraining cadence) — weight 10%

Owners / roles:
- Redwood: Marissa (SE lead) for integration and runbook; Aditya (solutions) for evaluation harness and offline scoring; me (Karthik) as deal owner and SLA point.
- Zenith: Claire (trial lead) for dataset provisioning and operator review access; Engineering contact for routing integration (please share name).

Next steps (action items):
1) Claire: confirm routing contact and sample volume by EOD Friday (2025-06-20).
2) Zenith: pick evaluation path (online shadow OR offline synthetic) — bold ask: please indicate preference in reply.
3) Marissa/Aditya: I'll schedule a 30-min tech sync immediately after Zenith confirms.

Attachments: pilot charter draft + proposed rubric (attached).

Happy to adjust cadence.

Thanks,

Hi Claire / Erik,

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of delivery notes and the SOC/compliance paragraph you requested (draft below).

Pilot cadence recommendation (adjusted to your 3-week preference):
- Week 0: onboarding + security review + routing integration (syncs + test tokens)
- Week 1-2: online shadow collection (target ~12k interactions)
- Week 3: offline scoring, manual QC of flagged cases, and acceptance grading against rubric

We think 3 weeks is workable for the signal you need provided the integration goes smoothly; we built in a short acceptance window in week 3 for additional focused checks.

Draft for SOC/compliance (paste into your ticket):
"Redwood will receive a redacted subset of live payloads for the duration of the pilot. Redaction is performed on Zenith's side prior to any network egress; fields containing patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN) will be replaced with stable tokens. All mirrored traffic will be encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and stored in ephemeral buffers with a 7-day retention for debugging only; logs used for evaluation are pseudonymized and access-controlled. Redwood personnel will only access raw payloads under mutually agreed escalation and with an explicit documented exception approved by Zenith security; otherwise evaluation uses only redacted outputs plus derived metrics. We can sign an addendum to the pilot charter that codifies these controls"

Evaluation specifics (technical):
- For online shadow we will capture model logits + top-5 span predictions plus a small evaluation header (latency, request size, model variant).
- For offline scoring we will run our evaluation harness against your labeled set and produce per-case JSON lines with the rubric scores so your team can re-run locally.
- Grading rubric example: we will compute weighted score (accuracy 40%, latency 20%, safety 15%, cost 15%, ops 10%). For edge-case review we'll provide a CSV of top-100 discrepant items.

Action items (owners):
- Erik (Zenith): confirm routing integration owner + provide test endpoints by Friday 6/20.
- Claire (Zenith): open security ticket with redaction implementation details; share SOC contact.
- Karthik (Redwood): confirm deal timeline and commercial terms (we'll prepare a short pilot agreement).
- Marissa/Aditya (Redwood): block tech sync — propose Thu 6/20 10:00am PT; will send invite once Erik confirms.

I'll attach a slightly updated rubric spreadsheet with scoring columns and example pass/fail thresholds.

—Marissa
